correction.text: Strongbow's Leinster (with Dublin) and Waterford, the Norman-held core when Henry II landed in October 1171

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Lordship. The page: Normans 'seized the important Norse-Irish towns of Dublin and Waterford' in 1170 and Henry 'granted Strongbow Leinster as a fiefdom' (Lordship article). The Cliopatria Kingdom of England shapes of 1210-1539 contain Irish land (modern countries include Ireland) and overlap this and later keyframes; the England dossier should subtract them. Infobox gives no area. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Leinster is now the seven counties kingdom-of-leinster loses in 1171 (Dublin, Kildare, Wicklow, Wexford, Carlow, Laoighis, Kilkenny); the gazetteer's 'Leinster' is the modern province and double-filled Meath (18 cells in 1171, against kingdom-of-meath to 1171) and Louth (4 cells, against airgialla to 1188).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Meath added in early 1172 ('In early 1172, Henry allowed de Lacy to take royal troops into Meath'). Treaty of Windsor, 6 October 1175, acknowledged Henry 'as overlord of the Norman-held territory'.

correction.text: Leinster, Waterford, Meath, east Ulaid (Downpatrick, from February 1177) and the Desmond grant around Cork (1177)

region.text: Waterford and Dublin, taken by the Normans in 1170 and brought under the Crown when Henry landed

ledger.note: 1171: Henry II lands at Waterford and the Norman conquests become a Crown lordship. 'On 17 October 1171, King Henry landed at Waterford with a large army of at least 500 mounted knights.' 'Fifteen Irish kings and chiefs submitted to Henry.' The Lordship article's infobox says 'Established: May 1177' (the title Lord of Ireland, given to John in 1177); the earlier start is the researcher's choice. Month: October. Dublin was the Norse Kingdom of Dublin (kingdom-of-dublin); Waterford, also Norse, has no dossier.

region.text: Leinster, granted to Strongbow as a fiefdom

ledger.note: 1171: Henry II grants Leinster to Strongbow as a fiefdom. 'Henry granted Strongbow Leinster as a fiefdom' (1171 section). Strongbow died in May 1176; his successor's claim rested on his marriage to Aoife (Norman invasion article).

region.text: Meath, the 'unconquered kingdom of Meath' granted to Hugh de Lacy

ledger.note: 1172: Hugh de Lacy takes Meath. 'In early 1172, Henry allowed de Lacy to take royal troops into Meath.' The Lordship article says 'Henry granted the unconquered kingdom of Meath to Hugh de Lacy' without a year.

region.text: Thomond and the approach to Limerick

ledger.note: 1174: Strongbow marches into Thomond. 'Strongbow responded in early 1174 by marching an army into Thomond and advancing towards Limerick.' The page gives the campaign, not the territory held.

region.text: Thomond and the approach to Limerick

ledger.note: 1176: Domhnall Mor Ua Briain retakes Limerick. After Raymond le Gros captured it, Domhnall retook it 'the following year' and 'burned it rather than have it in foreign hands' (Thomond article, which does not fix the year of the capture; 1176 is a bridge). The Treaty of Windsor of 6 October 1175 acknowledged Henry as overlord of the Norman-held land but did not end the Thomond fighting.

region.text: Desmond, granted to Robert FitzStephen and Miles de Cogan (without Thomond, which the circle touches)

ledger.note: 1177: the Council of Oxford grants Desmond to FitzStephen and de Cogan and makes John 'Lord of Ireland'. A grant, not a measured conquest; the Cork radius is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Ulaid east of the Bann: Downpatrick and the Antrim-Down coast

ledger.note: 1177: John de Courcy conquers east Ulaid. 'In February 1177, John de Courcy left Dublin with a force of about 22 knights and 500 soldiers' and 'captured the town of Downpatrick' in the kingdom of Ulaid.

region.text: Louth, the 'Uriel' of the Anglo-Normans: 'The Normans occupied the Louth area in the 1180s, forming the County of Oriel (Uriel or Vriell)'

ledger.note: 1189: the Normans hold Louth ('Uriel'). The Airgialla page says only that 'the anglicisation Uriel became the name of the part of Airgialla that had extended into modern-day County Louth' after the invasion, with no year; the County Louth page says 'The Normans occupied the Louth area in the 1180s' and 'In 1189, a royal charter was granted to Dundalk' (Bertram de Verdun). 1189 is the year airgialla's dossier uses for the loss; a bridge, confidence 1.

region.text: Connacht, whose remaining 25 cantreds Richard de Burgh held in chief of the Crown (without the five Roscommon cantreds left to Feidlim, drawn by kingdom-of-connacht as a vassal)

ledger.note: 1235: Richard Mor de Burgh conquers Connacht. 'It was only in 1235, when he summoned the whole feudal host of the English lords and magnates to aid him, that he finally expelled the Gaelic king'; Feidlim held only five cantreds (Roscommon) and 'Richard held the remaining 25 cantreds of Connacht in chief of the crown of England'. The Connacht article gives 1237 for the start of encastellation. Granted May 1227.

region.text: the five cantreds left to Feidlim Ua Conchobair in Roscommon

ledger.note: 1235: the Ua Conchobair king becomes the de Burgh lord's vassal. 'Felim was obliged to pay homage and was allowed to hold only five cantreds' (the page places them in Roscommon). Drawn in the lighter vassal tint inside the Connacht gain above.

region.text: Ulster, where Edward Bruce's invasion from Scotland began (the page names no zone)

ledger.note: 1315: Edward Bruce invades from Scotland. 'The Lordship suffered invasion from Scotland by Edward Bruce in 1315-1318, which destroyed much of the economy'; he was defeated at Faughart near Dundalk (History of Ireland 1169-1536). The zone Ulster is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Ulster, Bruce's invasion ended at Faughart near Dundalk

ledger.note: 1318: Bruce defeated and the invasion ends. 'in 1315-1318' (Lordship article); 'Bruce was eventually defeated in Ireland at the Battle of Faughart, near Dundalk' (History of Ireland 1169-1536).

region.text: 'virtually all of Ireland west of the River Shannon'; the Earldom of Ulster ended in 1333

ledger.counterpart: Gaelic and Burke lords of Connacht and Ulster
ledger.note: 1333: the murder of the 3rd Earl of Ulster. 'meant the loss of English authority in virtually all of Ireland west of the River Shannon.' In Connacht the Burkes split into Bourke of Mac William Eighter in the north and Burke of Clanricarde in the south (Connacht article). Ulster is the researcher's reading of the Earldom's land.

region.text: everything of the 1333 lordship outside the Pale: 'The English-controlled area shrank back to the Pale, a fortified area around Dublin'

ledger.note: 1348: the Black Death and the shrinking to the Pale. 'The English-controlled area shrank back to the Pale, a fortified area around Dublin.' 'after it had passed, Irish language and customs returned to dominance.' The Lordship article dates the Gaelic revival 'after 1350' and the restriction to the east coast 'by the mid-15th century'; the year is the page's, the land lost is the researcher's reading.
1361: the capital moves to Carlow until 1394. Infobox: 'Capital: Dublin Carlow (1361-94)'.

region.text: the part of Wicklow inside the Pale circle, in the Kavanagh kingdom

ledger.note: 1375: Art MacMurrough-Kavanagh begins to reign ('ruled from 1375 to 1417'); the kingdom 'continued to control much of what is today County Wexford and County Carlow' and parts of Wicklow until the early 17th century (Kingdom of Leinster page). The page gives a reign, not a conquest, so 1375 is a bridge (confidence 1). Mirrors kingdom-of-leinster's 1375 gain; the rest of that land was lost in 1348 (the Gaelic resurgence event) and is not drawn here after 1348. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Added to remove the double fill of the Pale and the Kavanagh shape.
1394: the capital returns to Dublin (end of the Carlow span in the infobox).

region.text: the Ua Conchobair remnant in Roscommon

ledger.note: 1474: the last Ua Conchobair king dies. 'From then until the death of the last king in 1474, the kingship was held exclusively by the O Conchobair's.' Whether the dependence of the remnant lasted to 1474 is not said; the end date is the end of the kingship.

region.text: the Pale and the English claim to the whole island

ledger.note: 1542: the Lordship becomes the Kingdom of Ireland. 'Crown of Ireland Act, 18 June 1542': 'This act declared King Henry VIII of England as the King of Ireland.' The Lordship article: 'The period ended with the creation of the Kingdom of Ireland in 1542.'

wars.name: Norman invasion of Ireland
wars.outcome: Normans take Waterford, Dublin (1170), Leinster and Meath; Henry II lands October 1171; Treaty of Windsor 6 October 1175; de Courcy takes Downpatrick February 1177; John made Lord of Ireland 1177.

wars.name: Bruce campaign in Ireland
wars.outcome: Edward Bruce defeated at Faughart near Dundalk; the economy of the Lordship was destroyed.

wars.name: Kildare Rebellion
belligerents: Thomas FitzGerald, Earl of Kildare (Silken Thomas)
wars.outcome: A failed rebellion; it 'served in the following decades to hasten the Tudor conquest of Ireland'. Dated 11 June 1534 (Thomas FitzGerald renounced his allegiance) in the Tudor conquest article.

certainty.note: The Lordship's extent is never described by a boundary in the pages; the English-held area is a patchwork of lordships, then the Pale (a ditch from 1494 only around parts of Louth, Meath, Dublin and Kildare). Soft throughout.

notes: Cliopatria has no Lordship; its Kingdom of England shapes 1210-1539 list Ireland among their modern countries, so the England dossier should subtract the Lordship's keyframes (or the renderer draw this colony tint over them). Typed colony: a dependency of the English Crown drawn as a lighter tint of England. No infobox area exists; the extent keyframes are the researcher's readings of the pages (counties named by the pages: Louth, Meath, Dublin, Kildare for the Pale; Downpatrick; Connacht). The start year 1171 is chosen over the infobox's May 1177 so that Leinster, Meath and Waterford are inside the life; the Normans' own conquests of 1169-1171 belong to Strongbow, not the Crown. Munster beyond the Desmond grant and Thomond are not covered by any page opened. Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-leinster, kingdom-of-meath, ulaid, kingdom-of-connacht, kingdom-of-desmond, Thomond, and the Gaelic lordships of Ulster (Tir Eoghain). The 1297 Parliament of Ireland is 'the high point of the Norman lordship' but moved no border. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] After the review: (1) {region: Leinster} (the modern province, 81 cells) is replaced everywhere by the seven counties of kingdom-of-leinster's 1171 loss, so Meath and Westmeath enter only in 1172 and Louth only in 1189; (2) new 1189 gain of Louth from airgialla (confidence 1: the Airgialla page gives no year, the County Louth page says the 1180s and a Dundalk charter in 1189), keyframes from 1189 carry Louth and airgialla is added as a predecessor. Thin gaps left: the 1176 contest end with Thomond (the Thomond page gives 1174 Thurles and 1175 Limerick but no year for the end), and the 1315-1318 Bruce contest has no mirror in kingdom-of-scotland (other group). [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Two double-fills found by the overlap check and removed: the Cork 60 km circle (Desmond grant) now excludes Thomond (3 cells of Limerick), and the 1235 Connacht gain and keyframe exclude Roscommon, which kingdom-of-connacht draws as the vassal remnant. The Pale keyframe (1348-1541) still touches the Kavanagh lands that kingdom-of-leinster draws from 1375 (6 cells); not subtracted. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] The Pale keyframe is split at 1375 and loses the Kavanagh lands from then on (loss cp kingdom-of-leinster, confidence 1), which mirrors kingdom-of-leinster's 1375 gain.
